newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds creep higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds creep higher in quiet trade.

text.p: Prices of U.S. mortgage-backed securities were flat to slightly higher, lagging their Treasury counterparts in most of Friday's quiet trading session.
Comparable Treasuries outperformed pass-throughs after market-friendly producer prices data alleviated some inflation jitters, one New York-based trader said.
Producer prices set the tone for Treasuries, he said. "Now it's as quiet as ever."

In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was up 1/32 at 99-09/32, yielding 93 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 1/32 higher as well, at 99-13/32 and 99-19/32, respectively. The 10-year Treasury note was up 1/32 at 96-25/32 bid to yield 6.70 percent.

The Department of Labor said the Producer Price Index (PPI) fell 0.4 percent in February, well below Wall Street expectations for a 0.1 percent loss. Excluding volatile food and energy prices, PPI fell a seasonally adjusted 0.1 percent. Wall Street economists were calling for a 0.1 percent rise.
